types.embedding_query_text: Cipher: A method of secret writing or a coded message. Also called code, cryptogram, encryption. Examples: Borg cipher, Copiale cipher, Borg.lat.898.

chosen_type.label: Cipher
chosen_type.definition: A method of secret writing or a coded message.
chosen_type.justification: No schema.org class fits ciphers; minting a new type under CreativeWork.

candidates.label: Barcode
candidates.comment: An ImageObject representing a visual, machine-readable code used for identification or data storage. Also called QR code, UPC code, data matrix. Examples: "The barcode on a grocery item", "A QR code for a website link", "A shipping label barcode".

candidates.label: EmailMessage
candidates.comment: An EmailMessage is a CreativeWork representing a message sent via electronic mail. Also called email, electronic mail, e-message. Examples: A business correspondence email, a personal email to a friend, a newsletter subscription email, a spam message.

candidates.label: Message
candidates.comment: A creative work representing a single communication from a sender to one or more recipients. Also called communication, dispatch, note, email. Examples: an email, a text message, a direct message on social media, a voicemail.

candidates.label: ComputerLanguage
candidates.comment: A formal language used for computer programming or other computer representations. Also called programming language, coding language, machine language. Examples: Python, Java, C++, SQL, HTML, XML. Distinct from Language, which refers to natural human languages.

candidates.label: Text
candidates.comment: A fundamental data type representing a sequence of characters. Also called string, character data, plain text. Examples: "Hello World", "123 Main St", "product description".

types.embedding_query_text: Library: A place where books and manuscripts are kept. Also called archive, repository, collection. Examples: Vatican library.

chosen_type.label: Library
chosen_type.justification: Vatican library is a specific library instance.

candidates.label: Library
candidates.comment: A Library is a local business that provides access to books, media, and information resources. Also called public library, academic library, media center. Examples: New York Public Library, a university library, a local community library. Distinct from LibrarySystem, which is a collaborative network of libraries.

candidates.label: LibrarySystem
candidates.comment: A LibrarySystem is an organization representing a collaborative network or system among several libraries. Also called library consortium, library network, regional library system. Examples: a state library system, a university library consortium, a public library district. Distinct from Library, which is a single physical or organizational entity.

candidates.label: Museum
candidates.comment: A Museum is a civic structure dedicated to preserving and exhibiting artifacts, art, or scientific specimens. Also called gallery, exhibition hall, cultural institution. Examples: The Louvre, Smithsonian National Museum of Natural History, local art gallery. Distinct from Library, which primarily lends books and media.

candidates.label: ArchiveOrganization
candidates.comment: An ArchiveOrganization is a LocalBusiness that maintains, preserves, and typically provides public access to archival materials. Also called archives, historical society, records center, repository. Examples: National Archives, a university special collections library, a corporate archive, a local historical society.

candidates.label: Room
candidates.comment: A distinguishable space within a structure, typically separated by interior walls. Also called chamber, compartment, space, area. Examples: a hotel room, a living room, a bedroom, a conference room.

types.embedding_query_text: Person: An individual human being. Also called individual, human, someone. Examples: Beáta Megyesi, Cecile Pierrot, Charles V, Michelle Waldispühl.

candidates.label: Person
candidates.comment: A Person is an individual human being, whether alive, dead, undead, or fictional. Also called individual, human, character. Examples: John Doe, Albert Einstein, Sherlock Holmes. Distinct from Organization, which is a group of people.

candidates.label: IndividualProduct
candidates.comment: An IndividualProduct is a single, identifiable instance of a product. Also called specific product unit, unique item, serialized product. Examples: a laptop with a specific serial number, a particular copy of a book, a unique piece of art. Distinct from ProductModel, which describes a class of products, and ProductGroup, which is a collection of products.

candidates.label: IndividualPhysician
candidates.comment: An IndividualPhysician is a medical business representing a single medical practitioner. Also called doctor, medical doctor, general practitioner, specialist. Examples: Dr. Jane Smith (a family doctor), Dr. John Doe (a cardiologist), a local pediatrician. Distinct from Physician, which is the general role, and MedicalOrganization, which is a facility.

candidates.label: Organization
candidates.comment: An Organization is a group of people with a particular purpose, such as a school, NGO, corporation, or club. Also called entity, institution, association. Examples: Google, Harvard University, Red Cross, a local sports club. Distinct from Person, which is an individual.

candidates.label: UserPlusOnes
candidates.comment: An outdated type representing a user's interaction of giving a "+1" endorsement, typically on Google+ or similar platforms. Also called user endorsement, +1, social recommendation. Examples: a user giving a +1 to a web page, endorsing a business, recommending content.

types.embedding_query_text: University: An institution of higher education and research. Also called college, academy, institute. Examples: Stockholm University, University of Oslo.

candidates.label: CollegeOrUniversity
candidates.comment: A third-level educational institution providing higher education. Also called university, college, higher education institution. Examples: Harvard University, Oxford College, Massachusetts Institute of Technology, Sorbonne University. Distinct from EducationalOrganization, which is a broader category for any educational body.

candidates.label: School
candidates.comment: An educational organization providing instruction to students, typically for primary or secondary education. Also called educational institution, academy, learning center, college. Examples: a public elementary school, a private high school, a vocational school, a university.

candidates.label: ResearchOrganization
candidates.comment: A ResearchOrganization is an Organization dedicated to conducting research. Also called scientific institute, research company, academic research center. Examples: Max Planck Society, Bell Labs, a university research department, a pharmaceutical research firm.

candidates.label: EducationalOrganization
candidates.comment: An EducationalOrganization is a CivicStructure that provides education. Also called learning institution, academic body, school. Examples: A university, a high school, a vocational college, a research institute.

candidates.label: HighSchool
candidates.comment: A HighSchool is an educational organization and civic structure providing secondary education. Also called secondary school, senior high, academy. Examples: Springfield High School, Northwood Academy, a local public high school.

types.embedding_query_text: ResearchInstitute: An organization dedicated to research. Also called research center, laboratory, institute. Examples: French National Institute for Computer Science Research, INRIA.
mentions: French National Institute for Computer Science Research

candidates.label: ResearchOrganization
candidates.comment: A ResearchOrganization is an Organization dedicated to conducting research. Also called scientific institute, research company, academic research center. Examples: Max Planck Society, Bell Labs, a university research department, a pharmaceutical research firm.

candidates.label: ResearchProject
candidates.comment: A ResearchProject is a Project representing a planned enterprise aimed at scientific or academic inquiry. Also called research initiative, study, academic project. Examples: a clinical trial, a grant-funded scientific study, a historical research project, a university-led exploration.

candidates.label: SearchRescueOrganization
candidates.comment: An organization dedicated to finding and providing aid to people who are lost or in imminent danger. Also called SAR team, rescue service, emergency search unit. Examples: a mountain rescue team, a coast guard search and rescue unit, a volunteer SAR group.

candidates.label: MemberProgramTier
candidates.comment: An intangible representing a specific tier within a loyalty or membership program. Also called membership level, loyalty tier, program status. Examples: "Gold Member", "Platinum Tier", "Basic Membership Level".

candidates.label: ITNonprofitType
candidates.comment: ITNonprofitType is a nonprofit type enumeration specifically for non-profit organizations originating from Italy. Also called Italian non-profit category, Italy NPO type, Italian charity classification. Examples: 'ONLUS', 'APS', 'ODV' (specific Italian non-profit legal forms). Distinct from NonprofitType, which is a more general enumeration of non-profit organization types.

types.embedding_query_text: Software: Programs and operating information used by a computer. Also called application, program, tool. Examples: Transkribus, ChatGPT.

candidates.label: SoftwareApplication
candidates.comment: A computer program designed to perform specific tasks for a user. Also called application, app, computer program, software. Examples: Microsoft Word, Adobe Photoshop, a mobile game, a web browser.

candidates.label: ComputerLanguage
candidates.comment: A formal language used for computer programming or other computer representations. Also called programming language, coding language, machine language. Examples: Python, Java, C++, SQL, HTML, XML. Distinct from Language, which refers to natural human languages.

candidates.label: OperatingSystem
candidates.comment: An OperatingSystem, as a SoftwareApplication, is system software that manages computer hardware and software resources. Also called OS, system software, platform. Examples: Windows, macOS, Linux, Android. Distinct from SoftwareApplication, which is a general application program.

candidates.label: RuntimePlatform
candidates.comment: A specialized software environment providing the necessary infrastructure, libraries, and services for executing a program. Also called execution environment, software platform, runtime environment, operating system. Examples: Java Virtual Machine (JVM), Node.js runtime, .NET Common Language Runtime (CLR), Python interpreter.

candidates.label: WebApplication
candidates.comment: A software application that runs on a web server and is accessed by users via a web browser. Also called web app, online application, browser-based application. Examples: Gmail, Google Docs, Facebook.

types.embedding_query_text: Conflict: A serious disagreement or argument, typically a protracted one. Also called war, battle, struggle. Examples: 30 Years' War, Thirty Years' War.

chosen_type.label: Conflict
chosen_type.definition: A serious disagreement or argument, typically a protracted one.
chosen_type.justification: No schema.org class fits a historical conflict; minting under Event.

candidates.label: DisagreeAction
candidates.comment: A react action expressing a negative opinion or difference of opinion regarding an object, proposition, or theme. Also called Express disagreement, object to, dispute, dissent. Examples: Disagreeing with a political statement, objecting to a proposed plan, disputing a fact. Distinct from AgreeAction, which expresses positive sentiment or agreement.

candidates.label: Conversation
candidates.comment: A series of one or more messages exchanged between individuals or organizations on a specific topic. Also called discussion, dialogue, chat, discourse. Examples: An email thread, a text message exchange, a forum discussion, a spoken dialogue. Distinct from Comment, which is a single remark on an item.

candidates.label: CreativeWorkSeason
candidates.comment: A CreativeWorkSeason is a distinct period or installment within a larger media series, such as a television show, radio program, or video game. Also called TV season, media season, series season, broadcast season. Examples: "Game of Thrones Season 8," "The Crown Season 4," "The Mandalorian Season 2." Distinct from CreativeWorkSeries, which is the entire collection of seasons or related works.

candidates.label: PoliticalParty
candidates.comment: A PoliticalParty is an Organization formed to contest elections and hold power in government. Also called political movement, party. Examples: Democratic Party, Republican Party, Labour Party, Conservative Party.

candidates.label: Claim
candidates.comment: A specific, factually-oriented statement that can be reviewed for accuracy. Also called assertion, statement, proposition, contention. Examples: "The Earth is flat," "Coffee cures cancer," "This product is 100% organic." Distinct from ClaimReview, which is the review of a claim.

types.embedding_query_text: Project: An individual or collaborative enterprise planned to achieve a particular aim. Also called initiative, program, undertaking. Examples: Descrypt project, Descrypt.

candidates.label: Project
candidates.comment: A Project is an Organization representing an enterprise, typically collaborative, planned to achieve a particular aim. Also called initiative, endeavor, venture. Examples: a software development project, a construction project, a research initiative, a community outreach program.

candidates.label: ResearchProject
candidates.comment: A ResearchProject is a Project representing a planned enterprise aimed at scientific or academic inquiry. Also called research initiative, study, academic project. Examples: a clinical trial, a grant-funded scientific study, a historical research project, a university-led exploration.

candidates.label: Consortium
candidates.comment: A membership organization typically composed of other organizations collaborating on a shared project or goal. Also called alliance, syndicate, federation, partnership. Examples: World Wide Web Consortium (W3C), a research consortium, a banking consortium, a joint venture. Distinct from Organization, which is a general grouping of people or entities.

candidates.label: Hackathon
candidates.comment: A Hackathon is an event where participants collaboratively engage in intensive computer programming or design over a short period. Also called coding sprint, dev challenge, programming marathon. Examples: university hackathon, corporate innovation sprint, open-source code jam.

candidates.label: DigitalDocument
candidates.comment: A creative work representing an electronic file or document. Also called Electronic document, e-document, digital file, computer file. Examples: A PDF report, a Word document, a spreadsheet, an image file, an e-book. Distinct from CreativeWork, which is a broader category for any creative output.

types.embedding_query_text: Artifact: An object made by a human being, typically of cultural or historical interest. Also called object, relic, artefact. Examples: Phaistos Disc.

chosen_type.label: Artifact
chosen_type.definition: An object made by a human being, typically of cultural or historical interest.
chosen_type.justification: No schema.org class fits a historical artifact; minting under Thing.

candidates.label: Sculpture
candidates.comment: A three-dimensional work of art created by shaping or combining materials. Also called statue, carving, monument, artwork. Examples: Michelangelo's David, Rodin's The Thinker, a modern abstract metal sculpture, a clay bust.

candidates.label: Product
candidates.comment: A Product is any offered good or service. Also called item, merchandise, offering. Examples: a pair of shoes, a concert ticket, a car rental service, an episode of a TV show.

candidates.label: ImageObject
candidates.comment: An ImageObject is a media object creative work representing an image file. Also called picture, photo, graphic, visual. Examples: a JPEG photograph, a PNG illustration, a GIF animation. Distinct from VideoObject, which is a video file, and AudioObject, which is an audio file.

candidates.label: MediaObject
candidates.comment: A creative work representing a media object like an image, video, audio, or text, which can be embedded or downloaded. Also called digital media asset, multimedia file, content object. Examples: a JPEG image file, an MP4 video, an MP3 audio track, a PDF document. Distinct from CreativeWork, which is a broader category for any creative output.

candidates.label: Person
candidates.comment: A Person is an individual human being, whether alive, dead, undead, or fictional. Also called individual, human, character. Examples: John Doe, Albert Einstein, Sherlock Holmes. Distinct from Organization, which is a group of people.

Also called Glossary, vocabulary, taxonomy, thesaurus, enumeration. Examples: The Dewey Decimal Classification system, a medical dictionary, a list of product categories, a set of industry standards. Distinct from DefinedTerm, which is a single entry within such a set.

candidates.label: MedicineSystem
candidates.comment: An enumeration representing different systems of medical practice. Also called healthcare system, medical tradition, healing approach. Examples: "WesternConventional", "Ayurvedic", "TraditionalChineseMedicine", "Homeopathic".

candidates.label: BookSeries
candidates.comment: A CreativeWorkSeries comprising a sequence of books published as a set or with a common theme. Also called book collection, literary series, saga. Examples: "Harry Potter series", "The Chronicles of Narnia", "A Song of Ice and Fire". Distinct from Book, which is a single volume.

candidates.label: Text
candidates.comment: A fundamental data type representing a sequence of characters. Also called string, character data, plain text. Examples: "Hello World", "123 Main St", "product description".

candidates.label: CreativeWorkSeries

Also called series, collection, franchise, saga. Examples: "Harry Potter" book series, "Star Wars" movie series, "The Simpsons" TV series, "The Legend of Zelda" video game series. Examples: a medieval illuminated manuscript, an author's handwritten draft of a novel, a composer's original musical score.
